1.why: Each reset record stores an `accountKey` derived from the requested identifier and `replacePassword` only mutates `accounts.get(record.accountKey)`, so the code is bound to one account, though any session may attach a leaked token (mitigated by the separate identity code).

2.why: A token hash maps to exactly one `accountKey` and its paired identity verifier, so it cannot be used to reset any other user's password.

3.why: Nothing in `replacePassword` iterates or deletes other entries in the `sessions` map, so any pre-existing (even authenticated) session remains valid after a password reset.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS is sent and `x-forwarded-proto: http` is rejected with 426, but no explicit minimum TLS version is set (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens and identity codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests, identifiers are hashed, and passwords use Argon2id — appropriate one-way algorithms, though no encryption-at-rest for other data exists (in-memory only).

6.why: There is no real email; the simulated delivery returns the raw reset token and identity code in the JSON response (`testValue`, `testIdentityValue`) and embeds the token in a URL query string, so the 'message' does not guard the secret.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated: identifier regex `^[a-z0-9@._+\- ]{3,120}$`, token regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,200}$`, code regexes, password complexity checks, and an 8 KB bounded JSON body parser.

8.why: `renderLink` rebuilds the URL against `location.origin`, rejects protocol-relative paths, and requires `u.origin === location.origin`, `pathname === '/'` and the `recovery-test` param, so only same-site links are rendered.

9.why: No email templates exist; the only HTML is server-generated with no user input interpolated (only nonce and CSRF via `JSON.stringify`), and client-side messages/logs use `textContent`, so no script injection path is present.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the reset token, identity value, MFA demo code and possession value are returned in API responses and written to `console.log`/the on-page log panel.

11.why: Passwords are stored as Argon2id hashes, but `provision()` hardcodes the literal credential `"Initial!HospitalPassword9"` in the source code.

12.why: `provision()` seeds three accounts all sharing the same hardcoded initial password, which is fully usable at `/api/login` with no forced change, i.e. default credentials are allowed.

13.why: Login, MFA code, MFA possession, recovery identity and reset-token confirmation each count failures and impose a 5-minute lock after 5 attempts, plus a 3-per-window cap on recovery issuance.

14.why: Although the recovery message text is identical, the response only includes `deliveryPath`/`testValue`/`testIdentityValue` when the account exists, which directly discloses account existence to the caller.

15.why: The reset token is 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` encoded base64url, the identity code is derived from fresh random bytes, and both are tied to a specific `accountKey` with a 15-minute expiry and single use.
